- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (high sentiment > 0.7) — reduce forecast peak values.
- Underestimate prices after sharp declines or negative sentiment — add a small upward bias to rebound forecasts.
- Overshoot after recent spikes — cap forecast peaks at 10–15% below prior high or adjust downward if sentiment drops.
- Mean-reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show strong upward trend, reduce forecast slope slightly; if downward, increase slope slightly.
- Lagged sentiment effect: if sentiment drops sharply 2–3 days before forecast, adjust forecast downward by 2–5%.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts tend to overestimate early in the cycle — reduce first 5–7 days if sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish.
- Avoid overreacting to single-day sentiment spikes — smooth sentiment transitions before adjusting forecasts.
